questions.expected: Making policy and laws that guide and protect tourism
questions.memo: Government sets the policies and laws that guide responsible, sustainable tourism.

questions.question: How do tourism BUSINESSES contribute to sustainable tourism?
options: By running responsibly, creating jobs and protecting the environment
By wasting resources to cut costs
By ignoring their staff and communities
By polluting as much as possible
questions.expected: By running responsibly, creating jobs and protecting the environment
questions.memo: Businesses contribute by operating responsibly, employing people and caring for the environment.

questions.question: Local _________ protect their heritage and benefit when tourism is run responsibly.
questions.memo: Local communities are role players who protect heritage and benefit from responsible tourism.

questions.question: True or false: Individual tourists are also role players in sustainable tourism through how they behave.
questions.memo: Tourists are role players because their behaviour can protect or harm the environment and communities.

questions.question: Sort each responsibility under the role player it BEST fits.

items.text: Set environmental standards for the industry

questions.memo: Government makes policy and standards; businesses run responsibly and employ locals; tourists behave responsibly.

questions.question: Which organisation certifies fair-trade, responsible tourism businesses in South Africa?
questions.memo: Fair Trade Tourism South Africa (FTTSA) is a role player that certifies responsible, fair-trade tourism businesses.

questions.question: True or false: When all role players work together, tourism is more likely to be sustainable.
questions.memo: Sustainable tourism works best when government, businesses, communities and tourists all play their part.

questions.question: A local community benefits from responsible tourism mainly through:
options: Jobs, income and protection of their culture and heritage
questions.expected: Jobs, income and protection of their culture and heritage
questions.memo: Responsible tourism brings communities jobs and income while protecting their culture and heritage.

questions.question: Setting laws to protect nature reserves and control development is the role of:
questions.memo: Government creates and enforces laws that protect nature reserves and guide development.

questions.question: A tour operator that trains staff, recycles and supports a local school is acting as a responsible _________.
questions.memo: A tourism business that trains staff, recycles and supports the community is being a responsible role player.

questions.question: Why is it important that tourists also act as responsible role players?
options: Their daily choices and behaviour directly affect the environment and communities
Because they own all the businesses
questions.expected: Their daily choices and behaviour directly affect the environment and communities
questions.memo: Tourists' choices — what they buy, how they behave — directly affect the environment and local people.

questions.question: True or false: Certification bodies like FTTSA help by recognising businesses that meet responsible standards.
questions.memo: Certification bodies recognise and encourage businesses that meet responsible, sustainable standards.

questions.question: Which role player is BEST placed to make national tourism policy?
questions.memo: Making national policy is the government's role, not that of individual tourists or staff.

questions.question: Local communities can support sustainable tourism by sharing their _________ and traditions with visitors respectfully.
questions.memo: Communities contribute by sharing and protecting their culture and traditions, enriching tourism responsibly.

questions.question: Which is an example of a business and a community working TOGETHER responsibly?
options: A lodge employs local people and supports a nearby clinic
A lodge pollutes the community's river
A lodge refuses to hire any locals
A lodge ignores the community completely
questions.expected: A lodge employs local people and supports a nearby clinic
questions.memo: Employing locals and supporting community facilities shows a business and community cooperating responsibly.

questions.question: True or false: If only the government cares about sustainability and no one else does, tourism is fully sustainable.
questions.memo: Sustainability needs ALL role players; government acting alone is not enough without businesses, communities and tourists.

questions.question: A tourist who supports responsible businesses and respects local rules is helping mainly by:
options: Rewarding good practice and protecting the destination
questions.expected: Rewarding good practice and protecting the destination
questions.memo: When tourists choose responsible businesses and follow the rules, they reward good practice and protect the destination.

questions.question: Which pairing of role player and responsibility is CORRECT?
options: Government — sets policy; businesses — operate responsibly; tourists — behave responsibly
Government — carries luggage; businesses — set national law; tourists — print money
Tourists — make tourism policy; government — serves meals
Businesses — set the exchange rate; communities — fly the planes
questions.expected: Government — sets policy; businesses — operate responsibly; tourists — behave responsibly
questions.memo: Each role player has a distinct job: government sets policy, businesses operate responsibly, tourists behave responsibly.

questions.question: Why is cooperation between role players the key to sustainable tourism?
options: Each plays a different part, and together they protect tourism for the future
Because only one role player matters
Because role players never affect tourism
questions.expected: Each plays a different part, and together they protect tourism for the future
questions.memo: Sustainable tourism depends on all role players doing their part together to protect tourism for the future.

TOUR.G12.T4.FEEDBACK.A1.title: Customer feedback & measuring satisfaction
TOUR.G12.T4.FEEDBACK.A1.description: The concept and purpose of customer feedback; methods to obtain it (surveys, questionnaires, feedback cards, follow-up calls, SMS messages, web-based responses); and how to analyse feedback — capturing the data, identifying common complaints, deciding on an action plan and starting an intervention — to measure customer satisfaction.
TOUR.G12.T4.FEEDBACK.A1.strand: Term 4 — Responsible tourism, customer satisfaction & marketing SA
TOUR.G12.T4.FEEDBACK.A1.recovery_strategy: Feedback is a cycle: COLLECT (surveys, cards, calls) → ANALYSE (find common complaints) → ACT (make an action plan) → IMPROVE (start the intervention). Collecting without acting changes nothing.

questions.question: What is customer feedback?
options: Information from customers about their experience of a product or service
A map of the customer's route
questions.expected: Information from customers about their experience of a product or service
questions.memo: Customer feedback is the information customers give about their experience, used to measure satisfaction.

questions.question: What is the main PURPOSE of obtaining customer feedback?
options: To find out how satisfied customers are and how to improve
questions.expected: To find out how satisfied customers are and how to improve
questions.memo: Feedback shows how satisfied customers are and where a business can improve its service.

questions.question: Which of these is a METHOD of obtaining customer feedback?
questions.memo: Surveys and questionnaires are common methods of gathering customer feedback.

questions.question: A short card left in a hotel room for guests to rate their stay is a feedback _________.
questions.memo: A feedback card is a quick way for guests to share their experience and rate the service.

questions.question: True or false: Follow-up phone calls and SMS messages can be used to gather customer feedback.
questions.memo: Follow-up calls and SMS messages are valid methods for collecting customer feedback.

questions.question: Put the steps of handling customer feedback in the correct ORDER.

items.text: Capture and study the feedback data
Start the intervention to improve service

questions.memo: Feedback is handled in order: collect, capture and study, identify common complaints, plan action, then act to improve.

questions.question: After collecting feedback, what should a business do with it?
options: Analyse it to find common complaints and act on them
File it away and never look at it
questions.expected: Analyse it to find common complaints and act on them
questions.memo: Feedback must be analysed and acted on; collecting it alone does not improve service.

questions.question: Studying feedback to work out how happy customers are is called measuring customer _________.
questions.memo: Analysing feedback lets a business measure customer satisfaction — how happy customers are.

questions.question: True or false: Web-based responses and online reviews are a modern way to collect customer feedback.
questions.memo: Online reviews and web-based response forms are modern methods of gathering customer feedback.

questions.question: Why is it useful to identify the MOST COMMON complaints in feedback?
options: They show the biggest problems to fix first
They tell you the exchange rate
questions.expected: They show the biggest problems to fix first
questions.memo: The most common complaints reveal the biggest issues, helping a business decide what to fix first.

questions.question: An 'action plan' from feedback is best described as:
options: A clear plan of the steps to improve the service
questions.expected: A clear plan of the steps to improve the service
questions.memo: An action plan sets out the steps the business will take to fix problems and improve service.

questions.question: Sort each item under whether it is a METHOD of collecting feedback or a STEP in analysing it.
questions.memo: Questionnaires, cards and calls collect feedback; identifying complaints, capturing data and planning action analyse it.

questions.question: True or false: Collecting feedback but never acting on it will improve customer satisfaction.
questions.memo: Only acting on feedback improves satisfaction; collecting it without action changes nothing.

questions.question: A guest fills in a questionnaire rating cleanliness, food and staff friendliness. This helps the business:
options: See which areas please or disappoint customers
questions.expected: See which areas please or disappoint customers
questions.memo: Rating specific areas shows the business exactly where it pleases or disappoints customers.

questions.question: The final step after planning is to start the _________ — taking action to improve the service.
questions.memo: The intervention is the action taken to fix problems and improve service after the plan is made.

questions.question: Why is customer feedback valuable to a tourism business?
options: It helps the business improve and keep customers happy and loyal
questions.expected: It helps the business improve and keep customers happy and loyal
questions.memo: Feedback guides improvement, helping the business keep customers satisfied and loyal.

questions.question: True or false: Online reviews can reach many future customers, so responding to them matters.
questions.memo: Online reviews are read by many potential customers, so businesses should monitor and respond to them.

questions.question: A questionnaire that asks customers to tick boxes and rate items is useful because:
options: The results are easy to capture and compare
questions.expected: The results are easy to capture and compare
questions.memo: Tick-box ratings make feedback quick to capture and easy to compare across many customers.

questions.question: Which shows a business using feedback WELL?
options: It notices many complaints about slow check-in and adds more staff at busy times
It collects surveys and never reads them
It deletes all negative reviews and changes nothing
questions.expected: It notices many complaints about slow check-in and adds more staff at busy times
questions.memo: Using feedback well means spotting a common problem and taking real action to fix it.

questions.question: Which statement best sums up the feedback process?
options: Collect, analyse, plan and act to improve customer satisfaction
Collect feedback and then ignore it
Only collect feedback from staff, never customers
Set the exchange rate using feedback
questions.expected: Collect, analyse, plan and act to improve customer satisfaction
questions.memo: The feedback process is a cycle: collect, analyse, plan and act to raise customer satisfaction.

TOUR.G12.T4.SERVICE.A1.title: Service differences & profitability
TOUR.G12.T4.SERVICE.A1.description: Reasons why the level of service differs from one organisation to another (training, staff attitude, management, resources, standards) and the impact of the service an organisation delivers on its business profitability — how good service builds repeat business and reputation while poor service drives customers away.
TOUR.G12.T4.SERVICE.A1.strand: Term 4 — Responsible tourism, customer satisfaction & marketing SA
TOUR.G12.T4.SERVICE.A1.recovery_strategy: Trace the link: good service → satisfied customers → repeat visits, recommendations and good reviews → more income and profit. Poor service → lost customers and bad reputation → falling profit. Service and profit are connected.

questions.question: Why does the level of service often differ from one tourism organisation to another?
options: Differences in staff training, attitude, management and resources
Differences in the country's time zone
Differences in the colour of the building
questions.expected: Differences in staff training, attitude, management and resources
questions.memo: Service quality varies because of differences in training, staff attitude, management and the resources available.

questions.question: How does GOOD service affect a business's profitability?
options: It builds repeat business and a good reputation, raising profit
It has no effect on profit
questions.expected: It builds repeat business and a good reputation, raising profit
questions.memo: Good service brings repeat customers, recommendations and a strong reputation, which raises profit.

questions.question: How can POOR service harm a business?
options: It drives customers away and damages the reputation, lowering profit
It increases the number of loyal customers
questions.expected: It drives customers away and damages the reputation, lowering profit
questions.memo: Poor service loses customers and harms the reputation, which reduces income and profit.

questions.question: Well-trained, motivated staff usually provide _________ service than poorly trained, unmotivated staff.
questions.memo: Training and motivation improve service, so well-trained staff generally deliver better service.

questions.question: True or false: The standard of service an organisation delivers can affect how much profit it makes.
questions.memo: Service quality directly affects customer loyalty and reputation, which in turn affect profit.

questions.question: Build the strongest argument for this thesis by choosing the strong supporting points.
questions.thesis: Good customer service improves a tourism business's profitability.

pool.text: Satisfied customers return and become repeat business
Happy customers recommend the business to others, bringing new income
A good reputation attracts more customers over time
The business has a colourful logo
The building is near a river

questions.memo: The strong points link good service to repeat business, recommendations and reputation — all of which raise profit. The red herrings do not.

questions.question: Sort each factor under whether it tends to RAISE or LOWER the standard of service.

items.text: Too few resources to serve customers

questions.memo: Training, good management, resources and a positive attitude raise service; their absence lowers it.

questions.question: A customer who receives excellent service is more likely to:
options: Return and recommend the business to others
Never come back and warn others away
Demand a worse experience next time
questions.expected: Return and recommend the business to others
questions.memo: Excellent service encourages customers to return and recommend the business, boosting income.

questions.question: Word-of-mouth recommendations from happy customers act as free _________ for a business.
questions.memo: Positive word of mouth is free marketing that attracts new customers and supports profit.

questions.question: True or false: Two hotels can charge similar prices yet deliver very different standards of service.
questions.memo: Even at similar prices, service can differ greatly because of training, attitude and management.

questions.question: Which is a reason one restaurant gives better service than another nearby?
options: Its staff are better trained and more motivated
It is in a different time zone
Its menu is printed in a larger font
questions.expected: Its staff are better trained and more motivated
questions.memo: Better-trained, more motivated staff is a key reason one organisation outperforms another in service.

questions.question: A negative online review about rude staff can harm a business by:
options: Putting off potential customers and reducing bookings
questions.expected: Putting off potential customers and reducing bookings
questions.memo: Bad reviews discourage potential customers, reducing bookings and harming profit.

questions.question: True or false: Investing in staff training can be worthwhile because better service can increase profit.
questions.memo: Training improves service, which can raise customer loyalty and profit, making it a worthwhile investment.

questions.question: Good management contributes to better service mainly by:
options: Setting clear standards, training staff and providing resources
questions.expected: Setting clear standards, training staff and providing resources
questions.memo: Good management raises service by setting standards, training staff and giving them the resources they need.

questions.question: Customers who keep returning because they are happy with the service are called _________ customers.
questions.memo: Loyal customers return again and again, providing steady income that supports profitability.

questions.question: Why might a business with poor service struggle to stay profitable?
options: It loses customers and gets bad reviews, reducing income
questions.expected: It loses customers and gets bad reviews, reducing income
questions.memo: Poor service loses customers and earns bad reviews, cutting income and threatening profitability.

questions.question: True or false: A positive staff attitude is one reason service differs between organisations.
questions.memo: Staff attitude strongly affects service quality, helping explain why organisations differ.

questions.question: Which chain correctly links service to profit?
options: Good service → satisfied customers → repeat business and recommendations → more profit
Good service → fewer customers → less profit
Poor service → more loyal customers → more profit
Service has no link to profit at all
questions.expected: Good service → satisfied customers → repeat business and recommendations → more profit
questions.memo: Good service satisfies customers, who return and recommend the business, increasing profit.

questions.question: Enough staff and equipment to serve customers properly are examples of the _________ a business needs for good service.
questions.memo: Resources — enough staff, equipment and supplies — are needed to deliver good service consistently.

questions.question: Which statement best summarises service and profitability?
options: Better service tends to raise profit; poorer service tends to lower it
Only the price, not the service, affects profit
questions.expected: Better service tends to raise profit; poorer service tends to lower it
questions.memo: Service and profit are linked: better service tends to raise profit, while poorer service tends to lower it.

TOUR.G12.T4.MARKETSA.A1.title: Marketing South Africa as a tourism destination
TOUR.G12.T4.MARKETSA.A1.description: The importance of marketing South Africa internationally (more foreign arrivals, greater awareness); the core business of South African Tourism; marketing opportunities such as ITB Berlin, the World Travel Market, the Tourism Indaba and the Getaway show; the funding role of TOMSA; and the concept of branding and South Africa's brand logo.
TOUR.G12.T4.MARKETSA.A1.strand: Term 4 — Responsible tourism, customer satisfaction & marketing SA
TOUR.G12.T4.MARKETSA.A1.recovery_strategy: Keep the roles straight: SA TOURISM markets the country internationally; TOMSA is the levy that FUNDS that marketing; the INDABA, ITB Berlin and World Travel Market are trade SHOWS where SA is promoted. Match each name to its job.

questions.question: Why is it important to market South Africa as a tourism destination internationally?
options: To increase foreign arrivals and awareness of South Africa as a place to visit
To reduce the number of tourists each year
To change the country's time zone
To raise the price of fuel
questions.expected: To increase foreign arrivals and awareness of South Africa as a place to visit
questions.memo: International marketing aims to raise awareness of South Africa and increase the number of foreign arrivals.

questions.question: Which organisation is responsible for marketing South Africa internationally as a tourism destination?
questions.memo: South African Tourism (SA Tourism) markets the country internationally as a destination of choice.

questions.question: Part of SA Tourism's core business is to market South Africa internationally as a tourism destination of _________.
questions.memo: SA Tourism works to market South Africa as a tourism destination of choice for international visitors.

questions.question: A large international travel trade show where South Africa can be promoted is:
questions.memo: The World Travel Market in London and ITB in Berlin are major international shows where South Africa is promoted.

questions.question: True or false: ITB Berlin is an international travel show where South Africa can market itself.
questions.memo: ITB Berlin is a major international travel trade show, an opportunity for SA Tourism to market the country.

questions.question: The levy that helps FUND SA Tourism's international marketing is known as:
questions.memo: TOMSA is the tourism marketing levy that helps fund SA Tourism's international marketing initiatives.

questions.question: Sort each name under whether it MARKETS South Africa, FUNDS marketing, or is a SHOW/event for promotion.
questions.memo: SA Tourism markets the country; TOMSA funds the marketing; the Indaba, World Travel Market and ITB Berlin are shows for promotion.

questions.question: The South African travel trade show that promotes the country and the southern African region is the Tourism _________.
questions.memo: The Tourism Indaba is a major South African trade show promoting the country and the southern African region.

questions.question: What is 'branding' in marketing South Africa?
options: Creating a recognisable identity, such as a brand logo, for the country
questions.expected: Creating a recognisable identity, such as a brand logo, for the country
questions.memo: Branding gives South Africa a recognisable identity, including a brand logo, used in its marketing.

questions.question: True or false: Successful international marketing can increase the annual volume of foreign arrivals to South Africa.
questions.memo: Good international marketing raises awareness and can increase the yearly number of foreign arrivals.

questions.question: Besides increasing arrivals, international marketing also aims to increase international _________ of South Africa as a travel destination.
questions.memo: Marketing builds international awareness of South Africa as a desirable travel destination.

questions.question: Coordinating the marketing activities of the many role players in the industry is part of:
options: The Department of Home Affairs' duties
questions.memo: Coordinating the industry's marketing efforts is part of SA Tourism's core business.

questions.question: Why does South Africa attend overseas travel shows like ITB Berlin and the World Travel Market?
options: To showcase the country to international buyers and travellers
questions.expected: To showcase the country to international buyers and travellers
questions.memo: These shows let South Africa showcase itself to international travel buyers and potential visitors.

questions.question: True or false: Maintaining and enhancing the standard of facilities and services for tourists is also part of SA Tourism's core business.
questions.memo: SA Tourism's core business includes maintaining and improving the standard of facilities and services for tourists.

questions.question: A strong country brand and logo help by:
options: Making South Africa instantly recognisable to international travellers
questions.expected: Making South Africa instantly recognisable to international travellers
questions.memo: A recognisable brand and logo make South Africa stand out and be easily recognised by travellers worldwide.

questions.question: The Getaway show is an example of an event used to:
options: Promote South African and regional travel to the public
questions.expected: Promote South African and regional travel to the public
questions.memo: The Getaway show is an opportunity to promote South African and southern African travel.

questions.question: True or false: TOMSA is a travel trade show held in another country.
questions.memo: TOMSA is the tourism marketing LEVY that funds marketing — not a travel trade show.

questions.question: How does increasing foreign arrivals benefit South Africa?
options: More visitor spending supports jobs and brings foreign-exchange income
It removes the need for attractions
questions.expected: More visitor spending supports jobs and brings foreign-exchange income
questions.memo: More foreign arrivals mean more spending, supporting jobs and earning foreign-exchange income for the country.

questions.question: Which pairing of body or event with its job is CORRECT?
options: SA Tourism — markets the country; TOMSA — funds the marketing; Indaba — a promotional show
SA Tourism — funds marketing; TOMSA — a show; Indaba — sets exchange rates
TOMSA — markets the country; Indaba — funds marketing; SA Tourism — a levy
All three set the country's time zone
questions.expected: SA Tourism — markets the country; TOMSA — funds the marketing; Indaba — a promotional show
questions.memo: SA Tourism markets the country, TOMSA funds the marketing, and the Indaba is a promotional show.

questions.question: Which statement best sums up the marketing of South Africa as a destination?
options: SA Tourism markets the country internationally to grow awareness and foreign arrivals
Marketing South Africa has no effect on tourism
Only foreign airlines market South Africa
South Africa is never marketed abroad
questions.expected: SA Tourism markets the country internationally to grow awareness and foreign arrivals
questions.memo: SA Tourism markets South Africa internationally to raise awareness and increase foreign arrivals, supported by TOMSA funding and trade shows.
